title: God's Official Takedown List
paragraphs: The Message of Amos, one of the shepherds of Tekoa, that he got on behalf of Israel. It came to him in visions while Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam II, son of Joash, was king of Israel—two years before the big earthquake.
Here's the deal:
God roars from Zion, his voice booms from Jerusalem! The shepherds' pastures dry up, and even the top of Mount Carmel withers.
God's Message:

"Damascus has messed up three times—make that four. I'm done with them. They pounded Gilead to a pulp, pounded her senseless with iron hammers and mauls. So, I'm setting Hazael's palace on fire and torching Ben-hadad's forts. I'm going to smash the Damascus gates and banish the crime king who lives in Sin Valley, the vice boss who gives orders from Paradise Palace. The people of the land will be sent back to where they came from—to Kir." That's God's decree.
God's Message:

"Gaza has sinned three, no, four times. I'm not letting it slide. They rounded up whole towns and sold them as slaves to Edom. For that, I'm burning down Gaza's walls and all its forts. I'll get rid of the king in Ashdod and the ruler in Ashkelon. I'll even go after Ekron, and what’s left of the Philistines will die." That's what God says.
God's Message:
"Tyre has messed up three, no, four times. I'm over it. They sold entire towns to Edom, breaking a treaty they had with their own relatives. So, I'm burning down Tyre's walls and all its forts."
God's Message:

"Edom has sinned three, no, four times, and I'm not having it. They hunted down their own brother, trying to kill him. No mercy, no heart. Their anger is just non-stop, 24/7. Their cruelty never takes a break. For that, I'm burning down their capital, Teman, and the forts of Bozrah."
God's Message:

"Ammon has sinned three, no, four times. I'm done. They literally ripped open pregnant women in Gilead just to get more land. That's messed up. So, I'm setting their capital, Rabbah, on fire, burning down its forts. There will be battle cries and war whoops, and a tornado to top it all off. Their king and his officials are getting dragged into exile." That's God's decree.

title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: God's Message:

"Because of Moab's three great sins—actually, let's make it four—I'm not dealing with them anymore. They went way too far and disrespected the king of Edom's body, burning it to ash. For that, I'm burning down Moab, burning down the forts of Kerioth. Moab's gonna go down with a lot of shouting and the sound of war trumpets. I'm taking out their king and all his officials along with him." That's a decree from God.
God's Message:

"Because of Judah's three huge sins—nah, four—I'm done with them. They totally ignored God's guidance and didn't follow my rules. Instead, they fell for the same old lies that messed up their ancestors. So for that, I'm sending fire to burn down Judah and all of Jerusalem's defenses."
God's Message:

"Because of Israel's three major sins—let's be real, it's four—I'm not putting up with them any longer. They're treating people like objects, buying and selling good people just to make some cash. They'd sell a poor person for a pair of sandals. They'd even sell their own grandmother! They crush the poor and push the unlucky aside. And it gets worse—everyone and his brother is sleeping with the same sacred prostitute, a sacrilege against my Holy Name. They have piles of stuff they stole from the poor at their god's shrine, and they're sitting around drinking wine they scammed from their victims.

"But look, I was always on your side. I wiped out the Amorites who came against you—men who were as tall as cedars and as tough as oaks. I destroyed them completely, from top to bottom. And yeah, I'm the one who got you out of Egypt, led you through the desert for forty years, and then just handed you the Amorites' land on a silver platter. I even picked some of your own young men to be prophets and set apart your best young people to be holy. Isn't that true, Israel?" God's asking.

"But what did you do? You made the trainees quit and told the prophets, 'Don't prophesy!' You guys are just too much for me. I'm so weighed down, I'm about to break. I feel like a wagon that's overloaded with way too much stuff, groaning and creaking.

"So when I finally make my move, what are you gonna do? There's nowhere to run, no matter how fast you are. Your strength won't matter. Your best fighters won't survive. Your skilled archers won't make it. The fastest runners won't escape. Even the chariot drivers are done for. The bravest warrior you have will end up running for his life, totally exposed and with nothing." That's God's final word.

title: God's Calling You Out, Israel!
paragraphs: Israel, listen up! God's calling you out. And yeah, I'm talking to all of you, the whole fam He rescued from Egypt. Listen!
'Out of every family on the planet, I chose you. So, because you're special, I'm holding you accountable for all your mess-ups.'

Like, for real, do two people just walk together if they're not even heading the same way? Does a lion roar in the woods if it doesn't have any food? Does a young lion get hyped if it hasn't caught dinner? Does a bird fall to the ground if it hasn't been hit with a stone? Does a trap snap shut if nothing sets it off? When the city alarm blares, don't people freak out? And when a disaster hits the city, you think God isn't behind it? God, the Master, does nothing without first telling his prophets the whole story.
The lion roared—who's not scared? God spoke—what prophet can just stay silent?

Announce it to the forts of Assyria, announce it to the forts of Egypt. Tell them, 'Get over to the mountains of Samaria and see for yourselves what a snake pit of brutality and terror it is! They literally can't do a single thing right.' God said it. 'They stockpile violence and blight. Therefore'—this is God's Word—'an enemy is gonna roll up on your country. They'll take all your power and raid your forts.'
Here's God's message:

'You know how a shepherd tries to save a lamb from a lion and only gets back a couple of legs or a piece of an ear? That's how little of the Israelites in Samaria will be saved—maybe a couple of old chairs, a broken table leg at best.'

'Listen up and testify against Jacob's family'—this is the word of God, the God of the Angel Armies! 'Peep this! The day I make Israel pay for its sins, for the fake altars at Bethel, those horned altars will be de-horned and scattered everywhere. I'm gonna wreck the winter palace and smash the summer palace—all your fancy houses. All those pretentious houses will be demolished.' That's God's decree.

title: God's Dropping Truth Bombs, But Is Anyone Listening?
paragraphs: Listen to this, you cows of Bashan grazing on the slopes of Samaria. You women! Mean to the poor, cruel to the down-and-out! Indolent and pampered, you demand of your husbands, 'Bring us a tall, cool drink!'

This is serious—I, God, have sworn by my holiness! Be well warned: Judgment Day is coming! They're going to rope you up and haul you off, keep the stragglers in line with cattle prods. They'll drag you through the ruined city walls, forcing you out single file, and kick you to kingdom come. This is God's decree.

God is saying, 'Go on then, go to Bethel and sin. Head over to Gilgal and sin some more! Bring your sacrifices in the morning and your tithes every three days. Burn pure sacrifices—thank offerings. Speak up—announce your freewill offerings! You guys just love showing off how religious you are, don't you?' This is God's decree.

'You know I'm the one who left you with nothing to eat, right? I'm the reason you had empty pantries and were standing in bread lines. But even then, you didn't get hungry for me. You just kept ignoring me.' This is God's decree.

'And yeah, I'm also the one who stopped the rain three months before the harvest. I'd make it rain on one town but not another. One field would get rain, and the one next to it would dry up. People were staggering from town to town, desperate for water, but never found enough. And still, you never got thirsty for me. You just ignored me.' This is God's decree.
'I hit your crops with disease and withered your orchards and gardens. Locusts devoured your olive and fig trees, but you continued to ignore me.' This is God's decree.

'I sent the old Egyptian plagues back on you. I killed your choice young men and prize horses. The stench from your camps was so bad you had to hold your noses. But you didn't even notice me. You just kept ignoring me.' This is God's decree.

'I hit you with earthquake and fire, left you devastated like Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a burning stick snatched from the flames. But you never looked my way. You just kept ignoring me.' This is God's decree.
'All this I have done to you, Israel, and this is why I have done it. Time's up, O Israel! Prepare to meet your God!'

Because look who's here: Mountain-Shaper! Wind-Maker! He laid out the whole plot before Adam. He brings everything out of nothing, like dawn out of darkness. He strides across the alpine ridges. His name is God, God-of-the-Angel-Armies.

title: God's Done with Your Fake Religion
changes: 2nd re-audit (Sep 24): ch5 p2 EN restored title "God's Word" (was 'the real deal'; KO already had 하나님의 말씀)
paragraphs: Listen to this, family of Israel—this Message I'm sending in bold print, this tragic warning:
'Virgin Israel? She's totally wiped out. No getting back up. She's just left there, and nobody's helping her.'
This is the Message, God's Word:
'The city that marches out with a thousand will end up with a hundred. The city that marches out with a hundred will end up with ten. Oh, family of Israel!'
God's message to the house of Israel is this:

'Look for me, and you'll actually live. Stop messing around with those fake worship spots at Bethel, don't waste your time at Gilgal, and don't even think about going to Beer-sheba. Gilgal's gonna be gone in a flash, and Bethel is all talk, no action.'

So for real, seek God and live! You don't want your life to be for nothing, just a pile of ashes from a burned-down house. Because God's gonna send that fire, and the firefighters will be way too late.

Woe to you who turn justice to vinegar and stomp righteousness into the mud. Do you even get it? You're in a universe created by God, with all these constellations. He's the one who wakes up the world every morning and puts it to sleep at night. He takes water from the ocean and gives the land a drink. God, the one and only, does all this. And he can wreck it just as easily as he made it. He can turn this amazing world into a total wasteland.

People hate hearing this stuff. The raw truth is never popular. But here it is, straight up: Because you walk all over the poor and literally take food from their mouths, you'll never get to live in those fancy houses you built. You'll never drink wine from the expensive vineyards you planted. I know exactly how much you've messed up, how huge your sins are. It's disgusting! You bully good people, take bribes, and kick the poor when they're already down.
Justice is a lost cause. Evil is everywhere. Good people just give up. Protesting and calling it out is pointless, a total waste of breath.
Seek good, not evil—and you'll live! You talk a big game about God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, being your best friend. Well, start acting like it, and maybe it'll actually happen.
Hate what's evil and love what's good, and then actually do something about it in public. Maybe then God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, will see what's left of you and show some grace.
Now, here's another message from my Master, God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies:

'Go out in the streets and wail! Fill the marketplaces and shops with cries of doom! Weep loudly, ‘Not me! Not us, Not now!’ Empty the fields, the shops, the workplaces. Get everyone in on the big cry-out. I want to hear it loud and clear when I show up.' God's decree.

Woe to all of you who are excited for God's Judgment Day! Why would you want to see God, want him to come? When God shows up, it's gonna be bad news before it's good news, the worst of times, not the best. It's like this: a guy runs from a lion and ends up getting attacked by a bear. A woman goes home after a hard day's work and is sexually assaulted by a neighbor. When God comes, it's reality check time, not some fantasy—a black cloud with zero silver lining.

'I can't stand your religious get-togethers. I'm so over your religious gatherings and festivals. I want nothing to do with your religious projects, your pretentious slogans and goals. I'm sick of your fund-raising schemes, your public relations and image making. I've had it with your loud, look-at-me music. When was the last time you actually sang to me? You know what I want? I want justice—like a whole ocean of it. I want fairness—like a river of it. That's what I want. That's all I want.'

'Israel fam, didn't you worship me faithfully for forty years in the desert, bringing the sacrifices I asked for? So how did you end up stooping to carrying around these lame statues of your so-called rulers, hauling around cheap images of your star-gods? Since you love them so much, you can take them with you when I kick you out into exile beyond Damascus.' That's the message from God, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies.

title: The Party's Over, Israel
paragraphs: Doom to you guys who think you're living the high life in Zion, thinking Mount Samaria is all that. You really think you're the top dogs, voted #1 best place to live. Well, snap out of it and look around. Get off your pedestal. Go check out Calneh. Then visit Great Hamath. And take a look at Gath of the Philistines. Doesn't that take you off your high horse? Compared to them, you're not all that.

Doom to you who are just sprinting toward disaster! A total catastrophe is literally right around the corner! Woe to those living in luxury, expecting everyone to wait on them hand and foot. Woe to those who only care about today and couldn't care less what happens to other people. Woe to the party boys and party girls who think life is just one big rager thrown for them. Woe to those hooked on feeling good—a life with no pain! And those obsessed with looking perfect—a life with no wrinkles! They seriously don't give a rip about their country falling apart.
But for real, here’s what’s actually coming: you're all getting forced into exile. You'll be dragged out of the country, whining the whole way, just a bunch of useless good-for-nothings.
God, the Master, has sworn it, and He's not backing down. The God-of-the-Angel-Armies says:
“I absolutely hate Jacob's arrogance. I have nothing but contempt for their fancy forts. I'm about to hand over the whole city and everyone in it.”

Imagine ten guys in a house, all dead. A relative comes to get the bodies for a proper burial, and he finds one survivor hiding in a closet. He asks, “Anyone else?” The answer: “Not a soul. But hush! You can't even mention God's name in this desecrated place.”
Listen up: God gives the orders. He's gonna smash the big houses into smithereens and the little houses into bits.

Would you ever race horses on a rocky field? Or plow the sea with oxen? Of course not! You'd wreck the horses and drown the oxen. And yet, you've made a shambles of justice, a bloated corpse of righteousness, bragging about your lame achievements, beating up on the weak, and crowing, “Look at me! I'm so awesome!”

“So enjoy it while it lasts, you Israelites. I'm sending a foreign army after you,”—this is your God speaking, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies—“and they're going to completely wreck you, from one end of the country to the other.”

title: God's Final Warning & A Prophet's Clapback
paragraphs: So God, my Master, showed me this vision. He was about to unleash a massive swarm of locusts. The first harvest, which was for the king, was already done, and the second round of crops was just starting to grow. Then, these locusts just devoured everything green. Not even a single blade of grass was left.
I called out, 'God, my Master! Excuse me, but what's going to come of Jacob? He's so small.'
God gave in.
He said, 'It won't happen.'
Then God showed me another vision. And whoa! My Master God was summoning a firestorm. It literally torched the entire ocean and then started burning up the Promised Land. It was intense.
I said, 'God, my Master! Hold it—please! What's going to come of Jacob? He's so small.'
God caved again.
'All right, this won't happen either,' God, my Master, said.
Then God showed me this vision: My Master was standing by a wall, holding a plumb line.
God asked me, 'What do you see, Amos?'
I said, 'A plumb line.'
Then my Master said, 'Check it. I've put a plumb line right in the middle of my people, Israel. I've let them off the hook for the last time. This is it!
'Isaac's sex-and-religion shrines will be smashed, and Israel's unholy shrines will be knocked to pieces. I'm raising my sword against the royal family of Jeroboam.'
Then Amaziah, priest at the shrine at Bethel, sent a message to Jeroboam, king of Israel:
'Amos is plotting to get rid of you, and he's doing it as an insider, working from within Israel. His talk will destroy the country. He's got to be silenced. Do you know what Amos is saying?'
'Jeroboam will be killed. Israel is gonna get exiled.'

Then Amaziah confronted Amos, saying, 'Look, prophet, get out of here! Go back to Judah where you came from! Do your preaching there. But no more preaching at Bethel! Don't show your face here again. This is the king's personal chapel, a royal shrine.'

But Amos stood up to Amaziah: 'I never set up to be a preacher, never had plans to be a preacher. I raised cattle and I pruned trees. Then God took me off the farm and said, ‘Go preach to my people Israel.’'
'So listen to what God is saying. You're telling me, 'Don't preach to Israel. Don't say anything against Isaac's family.' But this is what God is telling you:

'Your wife will be forced into prostitution in town. Your kids will be killed. Your land will be auctioned off. You will die homeless and friendless. And Israel will be hauled off to exile, far from home.'

title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: God, my Master, showed me this vision. It was a bowl of fresh fruit.
He asked me, “What do you see, Amos?”
I said, “A bowl of fresh, ripe fruit.”
God said, “Right. So, I’m calling it quits with my people Israel. I’m no longer acting as if everything is just fine.”
“The royal singers will wail when it happens,” my Master God said. “Corpses will be strewn here, there, and everywhere. Hush!”

Listen up, you who walk all over the weak and treat poor people like they’re nothing. You’re the ones saying, “When’s payday so I can go splurge? How long till the weekend so I can party?” You’re stingy and greedy, never doing an honest day's work. You totally use the poor, and when you’re done with them, you just toss them aside.

God swears against the arrogance of Jacob: “I’m keeping track of their every last sin.” God’s oath will shake earth’s foundations and dissolve the whole world into tears. God’s oath will sweep in like a river that rises, flooding houses and lands, and then recede, leaving behind a sea of mud.

“On Judgment Day, watch out!” These are the words of God, my Master. “I’ll turn off the sun at noon. In the middle of the day the earth will go black. I’ll turn your parties into funerals and make every song you sing a funeral song. Everyone will walk around in rags, with sunken eyes and bald heads. Think of the worst that could happen—your only son, say, murdered. That’s a hint of Judgment Day—that and much more.”

“Oh yes, Judgment Day is coming!” These are the words of my Master God. “I’ll send a famine through the whole country. It won’t be food or water that’s lacking, but my Word. People will drift from one end of the country to the other, roaming north, wandering east. They’ll go anywhere, listen to anyone, hoping to hear God’s Word—but they won’t hear it.”

“On Judgment Day, the lovely young girls will faint of Word-thirst, and the robust young men will faint of God-thirst—along with those who take oaths at the Samaria Sin-and-Sex Center, saying, ‘As the lord god of Dan is my witness!’ and ‘The lady goddess of Beer-sheba bless you!’ Their lives will fall to pieces. They’ll never put it together again.”

title: God's Final Word: No Escape & A Crazy Comeback
paragraphs: I saw my Master standing beside the altar at the shrine, and he said: 'Hit the tops of the shrine's pillars so the whole place shakes. The roof is about to crash down on everyone, and anyone left standing, I'm taking them out. No one will get away, no runaways will make it. If they dig down to the underworld, I'll drag 'em up. If they climb to the stars, I'll pull 'em down. If they hide out on Mount Carmel, I'll hunt them down and bring them back. If they dive to the bottom of the ocean, I'll send Dragon to swallow them up. If they're captured alive by their enemies, I'll send Sword to kill them. I've made up my mind to hurt them, not help them.'

My Master, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, touches the earth—a mere touch—and it trembles. The whole world is in mourning. The land swells up like the Nile when it floods, and then it goes down again, just like the great river of Egypt. God is building His palace with towers that soar into the sky, with foundations set on the rock-firm earth. He calls for the waters of the ocean, and they come, and then he ladles them out on the earth. God, your God, does all this.
'Do you Israelites really think you're better than the Cushites who live far away?' This is God's decree.

'Aren't I involved with all nations? Didn't I bring Israel up from Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Qir? But for real, you can be sure that I, the Lord and Master, have my eyes on this sinful kingdom. I'm going to wipe it off the face of the earth. But, I won't completely destroy Jacob's family.' That's God's decree.

'I'm still the one in charge here. I'm about to toss Israel into a giant sieve among all the nations and shake them good. I'm shaking out all the sin and all the sinners. No real grain will be lost, but all the sinners will be sifted out and thrown away—all those people who say, 'Nothing bad will ever happen to us in our lifetime. It won't even come close.'

'But also on that Judgment Day, I'm going to restore David's house, which has fallen apart. I'll patch up the holes in the roof, replace the broken windows, and fix it up like new. David's people will be strong again and will take over what's left of their enemy Edom, plus all the other nations under my rule.' This is God's decree. And He will do it.
'Yeah, for real, it won't be long now.' God's decree.

'Things are going to happen so fast it'll make your head spin, one thing right after another. You won't be able to keep up. Everything will be happening all at once—and everywhere you look, blessings! Blessings pouring down like wine from the mountains and hills. I'll make everything right again for my people Israel:'

'They'll rebuild their ruined cities. They'll plant vineyards and drink good wine. They'll tend their gardens and eat fresh vegetables. And I'll plant them, plant them in their own land. They'll never again be uprooted from the land I've given them.'
God, your God, says so.
